findings.title: New Diagnostics Content Pack in VCF Operations 9.1
findings.summary_md: VMware's Cloud Foundation blog announced a split between the Diagnostics Management Pack and a separate Diagnostics Content Pack, with vulnerability signatures delivered to the solution catalog instead of waiting for product releases. The first content pack includes findings for VMSA-2026-0006, covering the earlier vCenter Directory Service authentication bypass CVE-2026-59309, the Syslog server directory traversal CVE-2026-59310, and the VMXNET3 out-of-bounds write in ESX. The named signatures are vCenter_CVE_2026_59309to10_VMSA_202606 and ESX_CVE_2026_47876_VMSA_202606.

findings.title: vCenter Flaw Exploited Just Five Days After Disclosure
findings.summary_md: Infosecurity Magazine reported that QUIRSO observed exploitation of the July 29 vCenter advisory five days after disclosure, counting 361 victim IP addresses across 47 countries. The exploited bug was the Syslog server directory traversal CVE-2026-59310, rated CVSS 9.8, with attackers deploying the reverse_ssh tool for persistence. QUIRSO saw the first compromised systems contacting attacker infrastructure on August 3, and roughly 95 percent of the 361 IPs had appeared by August 5. Broadcom listed no workaround and fixed releases 9.1.0.0300, 9.0.2.0100, 8.0 U3k and 8.0 U2f.

findings.title: VMSA-2026-0009: Critical vCenter auth bypass (CVE-2026-123890, CVSS 9.8) plus SDDC Manager and VMware Tools fixes
findings.summary_md: A Veeam community post summarized Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0009, published the same day, as five CVEs in vCenter, SDDC Manager and VMware Tools with no workarounds available. It described CVE-2026-123890 as a CVSS 9.8 Directory Service authentication bypass requiring no credentials or user interaction, credited to Mandiant. The listed fixed builds were vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200, 8.0 U3m and VCF 5.2.5, with no public patch for vCenter 7.0 and an extended support request required.

findings.title: CVE-2026-123890: VMware vCenter · Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel
findings.summary_md: OffSeq's Threat Radar entry recorded CVE-2026-123890 with a CVSS 3.1 base score of 9.8 and fixes in vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200, 8.0 U3m and 5.2.5. Its data as of 14:21 UTC listed no CISA KEV entry, no public nuclei template or exploit module, and no attack traffic seen by its own sensors. The entry rated the vector as network accessible with no privileges or user interaction required and high impact across confidentiality, integrity and availability.

findings.title: CVE-2026-123890 vCenter SRP-6a Bypass: Detection & IOCs
findings.summary_md: Threadlinqs published a detection and IOC page for TL-2026-6463 covering ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus actor formerly tracked as UNC5221, and its use of CVE-2026-123890 against vCenter 7.x and 8.x. The page describes an unauthenticated SRP-6a session key disclosure over DCE/RPC on port 2012 that yields an administrator@vsphere.local session, and lists post-exploitation files including ActiveSer.jsp, u.jsp, /tmp/123 and /usr/bin/vmtoolscs. It recommends restricting ports 2012, 5480 and 22, rotating the vCenter STS SAML signing key, and forwarding logs off-box because the actor deletes on-appliance logs.

findings.title: Suspected China-linked hackers used an unknown VMware vCenter flaw, Google says
findings.summary_md: SecQuill reported, from Google Threat Intelligence research, that ARMORY CASTLE exploited CVE-2026-123890 as a zero-day in early September 2026, more than two months before VMware disclosed it on November 19. The report says the actor used port 2012 for the exploit, moved through an internal Linux appliance with the SLIMSAVAGE and CAGEMATCH web shells, used the BONESAW Go utility to copy the vCenter directory database, and used SAWSNAKE to forge SAML login tokens. It also notes a recovered BONESAW build date of July 13 and that blocking port 2012 from unapproved addresses would have stopped the exploit from reaching the vulnerable service.
